knowledge_point.title: Calculating the Slope of a Normal Line to a Curve at a Point

question.:question/problem:
Find the slope $m'$ of the normal line to the curve

$$
y=-x^{2}-5x-2
$$

at the point $\left(-2,4\right)$. Give an exact answer.

$m'=$
{{field-1}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=-x^{2}-5x-2$.

Apply the power rule:

$$
f'(x)=-2x-5
$$

The tangent slope at $\left(-2,4\right)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}
m=f'(-2)&=-2\left(-2\right)-5\\
&=4-5\\
&=-1
\end{aligned}
$$

The normal is perpendicular to the tangent, so take the negative reciprocal:

$$
\begin{aligned}
m'&=-\frac{1}{m}\\
&=-\frac{1}{\left(-1\right)}\\
&=1
\end{aligned}
$$

Let $f(x)=-2x^{2}-4x+1$.

Apply the power rule:

$$
f'(x)=-4x-4
$$

The tangent slope at $\left(1,-5\right)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}
m=f'(1)&=-4\left(1\right)-4\\

m'&=-\frac{1}{m}\\

question.:question/problem:
Find the slope $m'$ of the normal line to the curve

$$
y=2x^{2}-4x-1
$$

at the point $\left(2,-1\right)$. Give an exact answer.

$m'=$
{{field-1}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=2x^{2}-4x-1$.

Apply the power rule:

$$
f'(x)=4x-4
$$

The tangent slope at $\left(2,-1\right)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}
m=f'(2)&=4\left(2\right)-4\\
&=8-4\\
&=4
\end{aligned}
$$

The normal is perpendicular to the tangent, so take the negative reciprocal:

$$
\begin{aligned}
m'&=-\frac{1}{m}\\
&=-\frac{1}{\left(4\right)}\\
&=-\frac{1}{4}
\end{aligned}
$$
